newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says EMU policy unchanged by election.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says EMU policy unchanged by election.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Wednesday the Government would go into the election with its policy of keeping its options open over European Economic and Monetary Union unchanged.

Asked if the policy of keeping Britain's options open would remain unchanged up to elections which must be held by May next year, Clarke said: "Yes of course. I think it's a sensible policy." Speaking on BBC radio, Clarke also said he doubted EMU would go ahead on its proposed start date of January 1, 1999.

Clarke said he did not think it would be clear whether Britain would benefit from joining EMU until "we know a lot more about it. But this country is going to have to decide before long on the merits of it."
Clarke said EMU would offer the benefits of trade without foreign exchange fluctuations, lower interest rates and no transaction costs.

"But if there is a political charge on an unrealistic timetable to get a lot of countries into this EMU and they are not genuinely convergent...then I personally would be against it," he said. "But we must keep the option open of going in."
"At the moment we don't even know whether it will go ahead, we don't know which countries which will be in it. I don't think it will go ahead on January 1, 1999 necessarily," he added.
